source.style_reference_role: shared pixel-art quality, texture, lighting and rendering style only; scene/subjects not copied

composite_reference.role: visual reference only; not rendered when the state-driven object layer is enabled
composite_reference.prompt: Use case: game asset. Asset type: DEV scene background behind an orthogonal tile grid in a cozy farming adventure. Input images: Image 1 and Image 2 are style references only for shared high-detail pixel-art material work, polished crafted texture, warm natural lighting, rich controlled palette. Do not reproduce either composition or their subjects. Create an ORIGINAL forest map as strict orthogonal top-down 2D, camera directly overhead with no isometric angle, perspective convergence, or tilted objects. Landscape 3:2. A broad readable packed-earth path winds from a clear portal opening at the lower-left edge, crosses a small stream over a footbridge, and reaches a clear portal opening at the upper-right edge. Preserve open path width for tile movement. Large tree trunks and canopy masses, mossy boulders, deep water, and dense thorny shrubs should read as solid blocking landmarks; ferns, grass, wildflowers, berry shrubs and a small herb-gathering patch provide detailed non-blocking scenery and interaction landmarks. Keep at least two obvious walkable route branches. High-detail pixel art with crisp intentional pixel clusters, layered forest canopy, individually textured bark, moss, stones, plants and water, warm dappled sunlight and grounded shadows. Suitable to be used as a scene background under separate game grid/collision layers, not a tileset. No characters, animals, UI, text, labels, logos, border, photorealism, blur, isometric perspective, or copied assets.

state_transitions.tree: visible until chopped, then hidden over the clean background
state_transitions.forage: visible until picked, then hidden; existing daily world-change clearing restores it

prompt: Edit the exact high-detail forest candidate as a DEV base layer. Preserve 1536x1024 dimensions, orthogonal camera, creek, waterfalls, bridge, paths, lighting and palette. Remove trees, chop-able trunks, forage bushes, flowers, ferns, tufts and mushrooms, continuing natural grass/path/water textures. Keep rocks bordering the creek as static scenery; the DEV candidate map layout must provide matching collision where rocks block movement. The remaining interactive props are rendered from existing transparent game assets and MapDef/worldChanges. Not approved for production.

anchors_normalized_0_to_1.coordinate_origin: top-left; x and y are normalized to scene width and height
anchors_normalized_0_to_1.confidence: rough visual estimates only; all anchors are approximate and must be aligned to the target logical map grid before gameplay use

blocking_landmarks.label: stream and deep-water corridor (not walkable except bridge)
large tree trunks and canopy groups

limitations: Scene artwork is a DEV candidate only; approved is false.

The generated scene composite remains a visual reference; DEV runtime renders the validated candidate-layout with existing transparent forest art so visible obstacles, collision, chopping, and gathering share one MapDef.
The candidate layout and its art are unapproved and remain isolated behind the DEV Pixel32 preview query.
